Why go: a well-equipped catamaran for the southern islands

Victoria is set up for a day in the water: kayaks, paddleboards, a dinghy and snorkel gear are all on board, and the southern islands are close. Koh Tan's reef is about an hour away under sail, Koh Madsum is next door, and the full day adds the long quiet beach of Koh Rap.

Choose the option by your group's energy: the sunset sail for a short evening out, 4 hours for families, 6 hours for a relaxed day with lunch at anchor, and 8 hours to cover all three islands.

How the day runs

On the 4-hour morning charter you leave at 09:00, snorkel and paddle at Koh Tan from about 10:00, eat lunch on deck at noon and visit Koh Madsum's pigs before cruising back. The 6-hour version adds more time at each stop; the 8-hour day from 10:30 adds Koh Rap, a quiet island with a long beach. The sunset sail heads to Koh Tan at 16:00 and returns at 18:30. The crew speaks English, and a Bluetooth speaker means you can bring your own music. The south coast is the most sheltered side of Samui from November to January, which makes this a reliable choice in the windier months.

Who it suits

  • Families and groups of up to 10.
  • Kayakers and paddleboarders.
  • Guests staying in Lamai, Hua Thanon and the south.

Who should choose something else

  • Budget groups: our private longtail to Koh Madsum, Koh Tan and Koh Rap covers the same islands for less.
  • Groups who want meals included: the Red Baron cruises include food.

Good to know

  • Bring lunch: or pre-order the BBQ when you book.
  • Island fees: Koh Madsum and Koh Rap may charge small landing fees in cash.
  • Booking: online booking for tomorrow closes at midnight Thai time.
